problem: Deep RL navigation agents with LSTM, spatial-map or topological memory generalize poorly to unseen houses on semantic goals. Topological memories also assume pre-exploration, have no update operation, and cannot encode layout priors (e.g., kitchen is near dining room) learned from training environments.
motivation: Humans entering a new home head toward likely intermediate rooms (living room on the way from kitchen to bedroom). They do this using 'close-by' relations between semantic places that are shared across environments. A memory that stores such relations as probabilities can carry prior knowledge across environments, be updated cheaply from in-episode evidence, and support long-horizon planning without precise metric localization.
key_idea: Represent memory as a probabilistic relation graph over room types. Edge priors (Bernoulli 'close-by' probabilities) are learned from training houses and updated at test time by Bayes rule from co-occurrence of detected rooms in short trajectory windows. The graph is searched for the most-likely path to produce the next room sub-goal for per-target RL locomotion policies.
insight: Decomposing a long-horizon semantic goal into sub-goals via a Bayesian graph improves generalization, and the gain grows with more re-planning opportunities. At H=1000 BRM beats an equally-informed HRL agent with an LSTM controller by 41.1 vs 37.0 SR (57.5 vs 45.2‰ SPL); at H=300 the margin is 23.1 vs 19.9. Ablations: (1) the learned prior matters most at short horizon (uniform prior 20.9/39.4 vs 23.1/45.3 at H=300, but 40.4/56.6 vs 41.1/57.5 at H=1000), because posterior updates eventually wash out the prior. (2) Swapping in an optimal planner gives only 46.3 vs 41.1 SR, while an oracle locomotion gives 88.6, so the remaining error is mostly in low-level locomotion. (3) Frequent re-planning is key (N=10: 41.1, N=30: 29.7, N=50: 27.4 SR). (4) CNN-detected room labels perform on par with ground-truth labels (41.1 vs 41.7), showing robustness to semantic noise via ψ_obs.
method: Semantic classifier: a 10-layer CNN with BN encodes 4 panoramic views (for 'outdoor', the last 4 frames). Bilinear attention (W1, W2) weights the 4 features, then per-class sigmoid gives a multi-label K-dim room-type vector c_t. Test-time smoothing: a label is 1 only if confidence stays ≥0.9 for 3 consecutive steps. c_t=0 is treated as an extra 'unknown' node (K+1 nodes).

Probabilistic relation graph: each pair of room types has a latent Bernoulli z_ij ~ Bern(ψ_prior_ij) for 'close-by'. A noisy observation model gives y_ij ~ Bern(ψ_obs_0) if z=0 and Bern(1-ψ_obs_1) if z=1, with ψ_obs_0=0.001 and ψ_obs_1=0.15.

Prior learning: in each of the 200 training houses, run random explorations of 300 steps from rooms of type T_i and record whether T_j is reached. This gives 50 samples of z_ij per environment, and ψ_prior is fit by MLE. The prior is independent of the locomotion policy. ψ_obs is set by grid search on validation-house success rate.

Posterior update: every N=10 steps, bit-OR the buffered c_t vectors into B. Pairs that co-occur in B yield y_ij=1, pairs with one present and one absent yield y_ij=0. The posterior P(z_ij|Y_ij) is computed with Bayes rule, and the buffer is cleared.

Planning: find the path τ* maximizing c_t(τ0)·∏ ẑ_{τ_{i-1},τ_i} from the current room to the target over the posterior graph. The next node τ1 becomes the sub-goal g_t, and the agent re-plans every N steps.

Goal-conditioned locomotion: one LSTM policy per room target (a 'behavior' approach replacing gated attention). Each has 4 conv layers, an MLP of 256 units and an LSTM of 256 units, trained with parallel A2C (200 workers). Shaped reward uses geodesic distance decrease, with collision penalty 0.3, time penalty 0.1 and success reward 10. A curriculum raises max spawn distance by 3 m every 10k iterations, for 60k iterations total.
Termination variant: the semantic classifier doubles as a separate termination checker, which works better than adding a stop action.

setting.backbone: 10-layer CNN room-type classifier + per-target LSTM locomotion policies trained with A2C from scratch; non-neural Bayesian relation graph planner
setting.training_data: House3D (SUNCG) RoomNav: 200 training houses with GT room labels. RL for 60k A2C iterations. Classifier uses 15k positive + 15k negative samples per concept. Graph prior from random 300-step explorations (50 samples per z_ij per house). ψ_obs grid-searched on 20 validation houses.
setting.observation: egocentric first-person visual frames for locomotion; 4-view panoramic images for the room classifier (last 4 frames for 'outdoor')
setting.action_space: 9 discrete actions (large forward, forward, left-forward, right-forward, large left/right rotate, left/right rotate, stay still)
setting.privileged: In the main results, episode success/termination is checked automatically by the environment (no agent stop); Table 5 removes this. Otherwise none: no pre-exploration, and room labels at test come from the CNN (a GT-label variant is reported in the appendix).

numbers_note: SPL is printed in per mille (‰), not percent, and is kept as printed (e.g., 57.5‰ = 0.0575). Table 1 also gives per-plan-distance (1–5) breakdowns, not transcribed here. Figs. 6 and 8 give success-vs-distance curves only. Note that pure µ(θ) SPL values and Table 7 episode lengths are identical across H=300 and H=1000, possibly a copy error in the paper. Ablations (uniform prior, optimal planner/oracle locomotion, N=30/50) are in Tables 2–4.
results: On 5689 fixed House3D RoomNav test episodes in 50 unseen houses, BRM reaches 41.1% SR / 57.5‰ SPL at H=1000, beating the strongest baseline (HRL with LSTM controller, 37.0 / 45.2), the pure LSTM policy (22.5 / 22.9) and the semantic-augmented LSTM (22.4 / 23.8). At H=300 it reaches 23.1 / 45.3 vs 19.9 / 34.2. With self-termination (H=1000) BRM is still best at 17.3 / 23.0 vs 14.5 / 16.3, and its advantage is largest for targets several planning steps away.
limitations: Semantic concepts are a fixed, hand-picked set of 8 room types plus 'unknown', with one separate locomotion policy per target, so it does not scale to open vocabularies.

Low-level locomotion is the main bottleneck (oracle locomotion 88.6 vs 41.1 SR). Absolute SPL is very low, and the main results rely on the environment's automatic success check; with self-termination SR drops to 17.3.
Evaluated only in synthetic House3D/SUNCG houses with the paper's own generated episodes; there is no real-robot or standard photorealistic benchmark evaluation.
